blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings fell from 63 in June to 49 in September (−22.2%), and it took 15.4% of the city’s 188 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings was little changed, 15 in June and 15 in September (+0.0%), and it took 5.4% of the city’s 184 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Silver Valley for detached houses in July (a sellers’ best bet); condos and townhomes in June, July (a sellers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Lots and land in Silver Valley

items.t: Fee-simple lots are the default form: the sub-area's detached houses and large lots sit on fee-simple parcels unless title says otherwise: no strata corporation, no Form B, no strata fees.

The large-lot edge, as the feed states it (listing text only): the visible cards include a 5.29-acre property on 232 Street described in its listing text as not in the ALR with development potential, and a half-acre site on 141 Avenue described in its listing text with an Eco-Cluster Residential OCP designation.
Bare-land strata — none verified in Silver Valley
QUEUED — never counted, never presented as verified stock: the "Blacktail community" by Morningstar Homes: is named only in a feed card's listing text as a *neighbouring* community.

Lot character (sizes/zones), ONLY as the sources state them: Maple Ridge Zoning Bylaw No. 7600-2019 — RS-1 subdivision minimums are 668.0 m² lot area, 18.0 m width and 27.0 m depth, with maximum lot coverage 40%. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size. Which zones apply to specific Silver Valley parcels: UNVERIFIED — check parcel by parcel.
ALR vs non-ALR split: no split is published and none is stated.

Slope, watercourse and floodplain diligence sorts the hillside lots: the City publishes North and South Alouette River and Fraser River floodplain maps; which Silver Valley lots are affected is per-parcel: UNVERIFIED. Hillside/watercourse Development Permit requirements are likewise parcel-level checks — pull the City's maps for the exact address before removing subjects.

Assemblies / development proposals, documented AS SUCH, never as inventory: none is documented as a proposal in this area's research. The 232 Street acreage's "development potential" wording is listing marketing text (above), not a documented assembly or rezoning proposal, and no proposal is named or counted.

blocks.text: Streets, schools and getting around Silver Valley

items.t: The page is headed "Silver Valley Homes for Sale, Maple Ridge," with editorial copy, a market/census snapshot block and a live feed whose visible cards are all labelled with the board sub-area "Silver Valley" (232 Street, 141 Avenue and Bryant Drive among the visible streets).

Identity: this page maps to the SnapStats board sub-area "Silver Valley" in the Maple Ridge community, and the City's neighbourhood list names Silver Valley — the City describes it as sitting on the north side of the Alouette River and as a gateway to recreation areas with trail networks. Street-level board boundary: UNVERIFIED — no public street-level boundary was opened, and no City neighbourhood boundary was substituted for it.

Market context at sub-area level, labelled as such and never a land figure: Silver Valley, September 2026 — Detached 49 / 5 / 10% (joint with Albion); Condos & Townhomes 15 / 0 / NA (no attached sale recorded that month). Maple Ridge community context (NOT Silver Valley's figures): Detached median $1,131,000; Condos & Townhomes median $525,000. SnapStats publishes medians at community level only, has NO land category, and publishes no Silver Valley median: UNVERIFIED at sub-area level, as of September 2026, Source: SnapStats FVR/GVR September 2026 report.
Parks: Maple Ridge Park sits on the South Alouette River at 232 Street and 132 Avenue in Yennadon, with a playground, spray park and picnic shelter.

Transit: the West Coast Express stations serving Maple Ridge are Maple Meadows and Port Haney (weekday trains between Waterfront and Mission City) — both south-west of Silver Valley, not in it. Commute times in minutes: UNVERIFIED.
How people search for it: "Silver Valley Maple Ridge," "Silver Valley homes for sale," "homes for sale in Silver Valley BC."

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Silver Valley than in June?
faq.a: In Silver Valley, listings of houses fell from 63 in June to 49 in September (−22.2%); condos and townhomes was little changed, 15 in June and 15 in September (+0.0%).

faq.q: How big is Silver Valley compared with the rest of Maple Ridge?
faq.a: In September 2026, Silver Valley held 12.0% of the 410 houses listed in Maple Ridge and 5.2% of the 286 condos and townhomes listed in Maple Ridge.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Silver Valley from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 29 houses and 10 condos and townhomes sold in Silver Valley over those 4 months.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Silver Valley?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in Silver Valley?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: Can I buy a vacant building lot in Silver Valley?
faq.a: Lot-by-lot only — no named subdivision currently selling serviced vacant lots was verified. The built subdivisions trade as houses; the large-lot edge trades as individual acreage parcels whose designation, ALR status and servicing are confirmed per parcel.

faq.q: How did Silver Valley sell in September 2026?
faq.a: Medians are community-level only and are not Silver Valley's own.

faq.q: Did the Silver Valley Area Plan update change what my lot can become?
faq.a: The update was adopted November 25, 2025, and a feed card already markets an "Eco-Cluster Residential" designation in listing text — confirm the parcel's current designation and zone with the City before valuing subdivision or assembly potential; the listing wording is not the plan.

faq.q: Can I add a suite or more units to a Silver Valley lot?
faq.a: One secondary suite per lot inside the house, up to 40% of gross floor area and not in the floodplain area; eligible single-detached and duplex lots may have up to three, four or six units under the City's SSMUH bylaws — verify the specific lot's eligibility before valuing suite income.

faq.q: Is a large Silver Valley lot in the ALR or the floodplain?
faq.a: Both are per-parcel checks — ALR status on the ALC mapping (a card's "not in ALR" line is listing text only), floodplain status on the City's Alouette/Fraser floodplain maps. Slope and watercourse permit requirements are checked the same way, by exact address.
